findings.title: `WorkflowNavigator.ts`'s three sites are `SliceStatus.status`, not `NormalizedStatus` — the sweep contradicts the design's own exclusion
findings.description: Description: The Component Structure row (`:75`) and Migration Plan step 4 instruct "Replace 3 bare-string comparisons with `STATUS.*`" in `WorkflowNavigator.ts`. The three remaining literals in that file are two `slice.status === 'complete'` checks and one `status: 'complete'` assignment in `deriveSliceStatus()` — all `SliceStatus.status`, the workflow-position union. The file's `NormalizedStatus` comparisons are already swept by 241 (`STATUS.Complete`, `STATUS.InProgress`, `STATUS.Deprecated`). But `:49` and TD-3 (`:104`) explicitly exclude `SliceStatus.status` as "a distinct, larger workflow-position union ... touching it risks conflating two independent unions ... Left untouched." Following the migration plan would therefore implement precisely what the design forbids, making a workflow-position field appear to be a `NormalizedStatus`. Step 4's parenthetical "likely already imports `STATUS` per 241's TD-6 usage; confirm" also leaves a dependency unverified rather than resolved. Fix: remove `WorkflowNavigator.ts` from the sweep (0 in-scope sites), correct the site table and the `~65` total (`:41`, `:82`), and drop migration step 4 — or, if the intent is to sweep it, reverse TD-3 and the `:49` exclusion and justify the conflation.

findings.title: Success criteria and verification walkthrough are unsatisfiable against the documented exclusions
findings.description: Description: The FR at `:135` requires "No bare ... literals remain in production code outside `types.ts`'s own `STATUS` definition" and a grep "returning zero matches in the six swept files". That cannot hold by the design's own exclusions: `statusNormalizer.ts` (one of the six) must retain the alias keys `'in-progress'` and `'not-started'` (`:48`), which match the regex; `frontmatterSchema.ts` retains three matching literals; `types.ts` retains `SliceStatus.status`'s `'complete'` and the four `STATUS` definition literals. The command is also mechanically broken: `grep -roE` emits `path:match`, not `path:line:match`, so `grep -v 'introspection/types.ts:[3-6]:'` can never match anything. The walkthrough under `### Verification Walkthrough` (`:145`) computes "After: 4 ... + frontmatterSchema.ts (3) + SliceStatus.status (4)" — `SliceStatus.status` has exactly one matching literal, not four — and omits the two STATUS_MAP keys, so before/after counts do not reconcile. Fix: make the check explicitly whitelist the enumerated exclusions and assert the real expected count (add `-n` or drop the line-number filter). Related: `:51` claims "grep confirms zero `.test.ts` files assert against these literals directly", which is false — `taskFileParser.test.ts` asserts `.toBe('in-progress')`, `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts` asserts `{ value: 'in-progress' }`, `cli` list tests assert `.toContain('complete')`. "No test changes needed" is still correct, but the design should state that these existing literal assertions *are* the transcription-error detector instead of claiming they don't exist.

findings.title: "No public API signature changes" and the build-order constraint are incorrect for the `TaskFileResult` retype
findings.description: Description: `:43`/TD-1 (`:96`) widens `TaskFileResult.inferredStatus` from a three-member union to `NormalizedStatus` (adding `'deprecated'`). `TaskFileResult` is publicly exported: `packages/core/src/index.ts` re-exports `./introspection/index.js`, which re-exports `./types.js`, where `TaskFileResult` is an `export interface`. So `:84`'s "No public API signature changes" is false — this is an exported-type widening visible to CLI/MCP consumers — and `:84`'s "Consumer updates: none required outside `packages/core`" is justified by "`NormalizedStatus`'s type ... is unchanged", which is the wrong type to check. Separately, `:86`'s claim that retyping and sweeping `taskFileParser.ts` "must land together, or the intermediate state fails to build ... retyping alone would leave ... still-bare-string assignments failing to compile" is false: all three bare literals are members of `NormalizedStatus` and still compile against the widened field. Fix: acknowledge the exported type change, verify consumer impact (exhaustive switches or `Record`-keyed maps over `inferredStatus` in cli/mcp-server), or keep the original union and sweep assignments to `STATUS.*` anyway, and drop the fabricated build-order constraint. This is the one point where the design exceeds the slice plan's "pure mechanical refactor" without a corresponding test.

findings.title: Design is heavier than a mechanical literal sweep needs
findings.description: Description: The slice delivers one mechanism (`STATUS.*` references, already defined by 241) plus one optional type retype, yet re-argues the same two decisions three times: the Excluded bullets (`:47`, `:49`) → TD-2 (`:100`) and TD-3 (`:104`) → "Deferred to Other Slices" (`:128-129`). "Integration Points > Provides to Other Slices: None" (`:120`) restates `interfaces: []`, and "Consumes from Other Slices" (`:124`) restates Dependencies. The Verification Walkthrough adds a temporary-typo compile experiment and two live CLI smoke commands on top of `pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test` — for a byte-identical swap, the build plus full-suite baseline (`:141-142`) already covers both, and the typo check is a non-persistent one-off. The per-file site-count table (`:31-41`) is effort that is already inaccurate. Cut/consolidate: fold TD-2/TD-3's rationale into the single Excluded list, delete the "Deferred to Other Slices" subsection and the redundant Provides/Consumes lines, drop the typo experiment and live-command spot-checks, and replace the counts table with the enumerable grep rule. Keep TD-1, the migration order, and the baseline pass counts. None of these cuts drop scope the slice-plan entry assigns to this slice.
